item.research_question: Which elemental properties drive phase formation in AlCoCrFeNiTiCu high entropy alloys when inferred solely from chemical concentrations?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNiTiCu high entropy alloys (7 constituent elements: Al, Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Ti, Cu)
item.processing_route: Trained a feedforward artificial neural network (25-5-3 neurons, Levenberg-Marquardt backpropagation) on 225 experimental samples; generated 8,000 hypothetical samples using Algorithm 1 (min 4 elements, min 10% concentration each); developed primitive rules via Pearson correlation and pruned tree models (max 20 splits); optimized elemental properties using Genetic Algorithm (GA) with Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) or Euclidean space construction to maximize inter-group distance and minimize intra-group distance.
item.test_conditions: Dataset of 225 experimental HEA samples; 8,000 generated hypothetical samples; 23 elemental properties considered; GA optimization with mutation probability P_mutation; cost function defined by Equations (1)-(6) with penalty term for correlated variables.
key_findings: The neural network achieved an F1-score of 97.4% for FCC phase prediction.
The neural network achieved an F1-score of 95.6% for BCC phase prediction.
The neural network achieved an F1-score of 83.8% for IM phase prediction.
FCC phase formation in the AlCoCrFeNiTiCu family can be predicted with 87% accuracy using only the concentrations of Al and Cu.
Al exhibits a strong negative correlation with FCC formation, while Cu exhibits a strong positive correlation.
Genetic Algorithm optimization with SOMs identified electrical resistivity, molar volume, and electron affinity as the primary phase formation drivers.
Genetic Algorithm optimization with Euclidean space identified density, specific heat, and electron affinity as the primary phase formation drivers.
Electron affinity was the common property identified by both the SOM and Euclidean space methods.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that elemental properties responsible for grouping chemical elements into stabilizing (S) and destabilizing (D) sets for specific phases are the drivers of phase formation. They formulate an optimization problem to find the set of properties (e_opt) that maximizes the distance between elements in different groups (S-D) while minimizing the distance between elements in the same group (S-S or D-D) within a topological space (SOM or Euclidean).
item.limitations: The network architecture was not optimum, though it yielded satisfactory results. The IM phase prediction had a lower F1-score (83.8%) compared to FCC and BCC. The solution properties are believed to be a proxy to more fundamental properties on the atomic level.
quotes: FCC phase formation in the AlCoCrFeNiTiCu family of high entropy alloys can be predicted with 87% accuracy by only knowing the concentration of Al and Cu.
Genetic algorithm (GA) optimization results reveal that the phase formation is affected by the electron affinity, molar volume, and resistivity of the constituent elements.
The solution suggests that resistivity, molar volume, and electron affinity are the properties responsible for the phase formation in {AlCoCrFeNiTiCu} based HEAs.
